title: Dedicated GPU pool - autoscale/warmup debug scratchpad (7)
content:
TL;DR: intermittent capacity thrash in dedicated GPU pools during bursty job arrivals. Symptoms: rapid add/remove of nodes, long cold-start latency for vram-heavy models, requests queued and then evicted (OOM/eviction), warmup jobs not reliably marking nodes as ready. Suspect race between node labeling (warmup-ready) and autoscaler health checks + kube-scheduler binpacking behavior.

Chronology / recent incident notes (2025-01-12):
- ~09:03 UTC: Customer spike (batch load test) started, queue length spiked from 0 -> ~120 active requests in 2m.
- 09:04-09:08: Autoscaler triggered 6 scale-ups (requested 6 extra nodes). Nodes came up, but pods scheduled slowly; a subset of pods immediately went into CrashLoopBackOff with exit code 137 (OOMKilled).
- 09:09-09:15: Observed 3 nodes marked Ready then quickly NotReady/Terminated by cluster autoscaler; scale-downs started while other pods were still initializing. Result: more queuing and higher latency.
- 09:27: Warmup jobs started on several nodes but failed to complete because preemptible spot eviction policy removed the node mid-warmup.

Commands I ran (quick copy):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-gpus --show-labels --sort-by=.status.startTime
- kubectl describe pod gpu-worker-7f9b -n dedicated-gpus
- kubectl logs gpu-worker-7f9b -n dedicated-gpus -c warmup
- kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "gpu|dedicated"
- kubectl get events -n dedicated-gpus --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 200

Representative outputs (snippets):
- Pod describe: "Warning  BackOff  Back-off restarting failed container"; "State:     Terminated\n  Reason:    OOMKilled\n  Exit Code: 137"
- Warmup container logs:
  [2025-01-12T09:06:12Z] warmup: pulling weights for model-xl-16b
  [2025-01-12T09:06:45Z] warmup: loaded 65% of weights; allocating KV cache...
  [2025-01-12T09:07:10Z] warmup: allocation failed: could not reserve 6GB GPU memory (available: 4.1GB)
  [2025-01-12T09:07:11Z] warmup: exiting with OOM
- Node events: "Instance termination requested by cloud provider (preemptible)" and "Node has insufficient memory to schedule pod"

Observations / hypotheses so far:
1) Warmup jobs are getting scheduled on nodes before the node has the full required GPU memory available (either due to other system pods or because device plugins haven't finished initializing), leading to OOM or allocation failure. The scheduler then evicts/terminates pods -> autoscaler sees low utilization and scales down, causing thrash.
2) Spot/preemptible instance eviction amplifies the problem: warmups are long running (tens of seconds to minutes), so if spot eviction happens mid-warmup, the node is killed and we waste warmup work.
3) Node labeling for "warmup-ready" is racing with kubelet/device-plugin registration. Our warmup controller relies on a node label to consider a node ready to receive warmup traffic; if label applied too early or too late we either run warmups prematurely or wait too long, both impacting latency and utilization.
4) Autoscaler scale-down policy might be too aggressive (short grace period) and doesn't consider nodes with in-progress warmup jobs as protected.
5) Packing policy: scheduler tries to binpack pods, sometimes putting multiple heavy warmup pods onto same physical GPU (or same node with limited VRAM), causing OOMs. Might be affinity/anti-affinity config missing for warmup pods.

Things I tried (and results):
- Increase warmup pod resource requests (gpu-mem-request annotation) to better express real memory needs -> reduced OOM by ~30% in staging, but still occasional fails because available memory decreased by other system daemons.
- Add a pre-scheduling check (initContainer) that queries nvidia-smi to ensure free memory > threshold before starting heavy model loads -> worked for catching some cases, but initContainer still allocated trivial GPU memory and then scheduler sometimes drained node before warmup finished.
- Simulated spot eviction in staging: when eviction occurs, no graceful drain of warmup pods occurs (we rely on cloud provider to send SIGTERM). Warmup cleanup is not robust.
- Tweaked cluster autoscaler config: bumping scaleDownUnneededTime to 10m reduced immediate scale-downs, but increased cost and delayed reclaim of genuinely unused capacity. Partial improvement.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there any device-plugin bugs where memory reported as available is optimistic and actual allocation fails? We saw "could not reserve 6GB" while nvidia-smi reported 7GB free in one case. Need to correlate driver times.
- Does our warmup controller mark node ready via label BEFORE kubelet has registered GPU devices? Need to add strong gating: wait for device plugin and a small probe.
- What's the median warmup time per model variant at current model size/quantization? We should capture distribution (p50/p90/p99).

Immediate next steps (prioritized):
1) Add node-probe gating: warmup controller should wait for kubelet/device-plugin annotation (e.g., 'nvidia.com/gpu-present=true') and a small probe that runs a memory allocation test before placing heavy warmup tasks. (Owner: Priya)
2) Protect nodes with in-progress warmup from scale-down: mark them with annotation "warmup-in-progress=true" and extend scaleDownUnneededTime for those nodes in autoscaler config (or use CA expander hook). (Owner: Jamal)
3) Introduce warmup pod anti-affinity (soft preferredDuringScheduling to avoid packing >1 warmup per GPU). (Owner: Aisha)
4) Implement warmup checkpointing: if warmup is interrupted, we should mark model shards cached in central artifact store or use a pre-warmed disk snapshot to reduce re-warmup costs. (Investigate feasibility)
5) Add better observability: warmup success/failure metric, warmup duration per node, per-model warmup memory allocations, and spot-eviction correlation. Create dashboard and alert when warmup failure rate > 5%.

Longer-term ideas:
- Use a separate node class for warmup-friendly instances (non-preemptible, slightly higher memory) and route warmup jobs there; keep them as warm pool. Cost tradeoff but much more stable.
- Opportunistic lightweight warmup: prefetch model heads but avoid full KV cache until node is fully stable. Could reduce wasted VRAM.

Notes on reproductions done in staging:
- Test scenario: bursty arrival simulated by loadgen (100->200 concurrent) with short bursts (1-3m) -> reproduced thrash when scaleDownUnneededTime < 5m and warmup median > 60s.
- Logs attached to linked artifacts (INF-3482).

Short checklist for a quick mitigation deploy (safe changes):
- [ ] Increase scaleDownUnneededTime to 8m (pilot)
- [ ] Add warmup-in-progress node annotation in warmup controller
- [ ] Add a simple nvidia-smi initContainer probe in warmup pod spec
- [ ] Create Cloudwatch/Stackdriver alert for warmup-failure-rate > 5%

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight; copy to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/ when we have a writeup for team. Follow-up meeting with infra + CA owners tomorrow 2025-01-15.

-- Aisha
